Its precise force in any particular verse depends on the surrounding passage.

Besodeiah is a personal name, referring to one individual rather than describing an action, object, or quality. This Hebrew verb means “boiled.” It describes food being cooked in liquid, or the action of bringing food to that state. Its use therefore centers on a practical cooking action rather than a person, object, or abstract idea. The exact force in a particular verse depends on the surrounding sentence and passage.

This Hebrew noun means “cubit,” a unit used to measure length. It refers to a standard distance rather than an action, person, or quality. Its basic meaning remains a measured length, allowing the reader to understand it as a physical measurement used in describing an object or distance.

Uel is a Hebrew personal name, referring to an individual rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. Thus, readers should understand H1813 as a proper name used to identify a person, not as a descriptive Hebrew term.
